title: Tail chunking and deferred-free patterns — OOM/root-cause notes
content:
Summary:
We repeatedly hit OOM in multi-tenant inference pools under realistic traffic spikes. Root cause is not a single oversized allocation but a combination of (1) tail-chunking — many small leftover fragments at the end of arenas, (2) deferred/free aggregation semantics of cudaFreeAsync/cudamallocasync which keep memory accounted as "in-use" until stream work drains, and (3) workspace warmup patterns that transiently allocate large contiguous buffers on rare code paths. These interact to create temporary but high peak working set that exceeds arena/reservation thresholds and triggers OOMs.

Why this doc exists and scope:
- Capture a reproducible scenario and allocator traces for the team.
- Record experiments run and mitigations that worked in staging.
- Recommend engineering/ops fixes and short-term risk mitigations for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Environment & baseline:
- Runtime: inference-runtime v0.78.3 (branch: fix/oom-investigations)
- CUDA: 11.8, driver 535.54.03
- Allocator: custom arena-based allocator built on top of cudamallocasync (pool manager + per-stream deferred-free queues)
- GPU instance: p4d-like 8xA100 equivalent, 80GB device memory (logical test with 64GB reserved for runtime)
- Workload: mixed short-chat (seq_len <= 128) + long prompt generation (seq_len up to 4096) at 70/30 ratio, bursty traffic (sustained 200 req/s for 30s in reproduction)
- Baseline measured peak before mitigations: 61.7 GB used (OOM triggered at ~62 GB)

Observed symptoms:
- Out-of-memory (OOM) occurs intermittently ~10–15 minutes after high-variance burst.
- Heap map shows large number of small free segments localized to the tail of arenas, while head of arenas contains large live allocations.
- CUDA API traces show cudaFreeAsync calls that do not result in immediate cudamallocasync reuse; memory appears as "pending free" in allocator counters until stream sync or batched drain.
- Reproduces reliably by mixing many short-lived tensors between long-lived KV-cache allocations.

Key hypothesis (short):
1) Many short allocations create tail fragments that cannot be coalesced with earlier freed blocks because allocator rounds/aligns and keeps per-arena free lists per size-class.
2) cudaFreeAsync semantics + per-stream deferred-free queues mean freed chunks are not returned to global reuse promptly; under bursty, cross-stream reuse patterns they accumulate and push arena high-water mark beyond reserved threshold.
3) A rare workspace allocation (e.g., fused-attention temporary) performs a contiguous large allocation and fails due to fragmentation even though total free cumulative space across arenas would be enough if coalesced.

Repro steps (condensed):
1) Start runtime with --allocator=async-pool --arena-reservation 62GB --enable-stream-caching
2) Run traffic generator (tg.py) that issues 70% short (seq <= 128) and 30% long (seq 2048–4096) requests in bursts: python tg.py --qps 200 --burst 30 --mix short:long=70:30
3) Observe OOM in logs after ~25–40s of burst; dump allocator state via /debug/allocator/state endpoint.

Allocator snapshot (abridged):
- arenas: 4
- arena[3] high_water_mark: 63.1GB
- arena[3] free_list_small_bins: 10240 entries (0.5–4KB)
- arena[3] tail_fragments: 14 entries (sizes: 96KB, 128KB, 176KB, 320KB, 512KB, others)
- pending_free_queue (per-stream totals): s0: 1.2GB, s1: 0.9GB, s2: 0.0GB, s3: 2.6GB (pending until stream drains)
- global_freeable_but_deferred: 4.7GB

Important trace snippet (from CUPTI-like trace):
[2025-10-21T15:03:02Z] stream s3: cudaMallocAsync(ptr=0x7f12..., size=48MB) -> SUCCESS
[2025-10-21T15:03:04Z] stream s1: cudaFreeAsync(ptr=0x7f12..., stream=s1) -> QUEUED (deferred)
[2025-10-21T15:03:05Z] stream s3: cudaMallocAsync(ptr=0x7f15..., size=56MB) -> SUCCESS (from new tail region)
[2025-10-21T15:03:06Z] stream s0: cudaFreeAsync(ptr=0x7f10..., stream=s0) -> QUEUED
[2025-10-21T15:03:07Z] stream s3: attempt cudaMallocAsync(size=120MB) -> FAIL (OOM)

From these traces we see allocations and frees are aligned to per-stream deferred queues and new allocations proceed from tail causing fragmentation. The allocator will not coalesce across pending frees.

Experiments & results:
- EXP-01: Reduce arena count from 4->2 and increase arena size (64GB->80GB cap).
  - Result: Delays OOM but still fails under same burst pattern. Peak decreased by ~3GB but fragmentation persists.
- EXP-02: Force synchronous frees on high-memory paths (cudaFree instead of cudaFreeAsync) for workspace allocations only.
  - Result: Peak memory dropped to 52.6GB, no OOM in 10/10 runs. Latency impact: median +6ms on long requests.
- EXP-03: Introduce eager coalesce: drain pending-free queues on allocation miss that requests contiguous large block (only for >32MB allocation).
  - Result: Peak memory 44.3GB, no OOM; small CPU overhead (~0.5% CPU). This is our best short-term mitigation.
- EXP-04: Pre-allocate a dedicated fixed workspace slab for fused-attention paths (reserve 128MB aligned blocks).
  - Result: Eliminated failure on that particular path; overall peak ~47.1GB. Requires per-model config to size slab.
- EXP-05: Change size-class granularity to coarser bins to reduce tail-fragmentation.
  - Result: Mixed results: slightly lower fragmentation but higher internal waste; overall peak ~49.8GB. Increased average memory consumption for long-running models.

Why eager coalesce helps:
- Triggered when allocation miss occurs for a large contiguous request (>32MB): we scan per-stream deferred-free queues and attempt to reclaim/race the pending frees by issuing a blocking stream synchronization only to drain small number of streams (configurable max streams scanned). This reclaims large contiguous regions without globally forcing synchronous frees for every allocation. Tradeoff: possible additional latency for a small fraction of allocations and starve detection complexity.

Short-term mitigations (recommended for next deploy):
1) Roll out eager-coalesce on canary nodes behind feature flag (runtime flag: --eager-coalesce=enabled; threshold=32MB; max-stream-scan=3). Verified stable in staging.
2) Change critical workspace code-paths to use synchronous free (cudaFree) or dedicated slab pools (configurable per-model). Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/998
3) Add telemetry: expose pending_free_queue size per-stream to metrics (prometheus histograms) and raise alerts when global_deferred > 2GB for >60s.
4) Lower default arena-reservation by 5% to force earlier GC-like reclaiming activities; monitor for regressions.

Medium-term changes (design notes):
- Implement cross-stream deferred-free merging: maintain a lightweight background reclaimer thread that drains deferred frees opportunistically based on free-space pressure rather than blocking allocations.
- Revisit binning strategy: move to hybrid size-classing where very common small sizes use power-of-two slab pools (zero fragmentation) while mid/large sizes use coarse bins.
- Profile and reduce workspace allocation variance: refactor fused kernels and memory planning to avoid occasional large contiguous allocations wherever possible.

Operational playbook (on-call):
1) If OOMs spike, check /debug/allocator/state and gauge pending_free_queue.
2) If global deferred > 2GB and immediate demand high, toggle --eager-coalesce=enabled on the pool (hot restart supported) and monitor.
3) As a last resort, drain streams by graceful node restart (edge case only).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- We still see a low-probability case where two simultaneous large allocations both fail due to ordering of pending frees across different streams; need deterministic reproducer.
- Edge case with pinned host staging buffers: are we undercounting pinned host memory that contributes to fragmentation? Investigate via nvml stats.
- Interaction with cuBLAS/cuDNN internal workspace allocations: need to capture library-internal allocations (via MPS/cupti) to see if they request contiguous blocks that fragment arenas unexpectedly.

Appendix: useful commands & traces
- Dump allocator state (local dev): curl localhost:8080/debug/allocator/state | jq . > alloc-state.json
- Nsight Systems sampling: nsys profile -o nsight-repro --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --capture-range=cudaRuntimeApi -- ./bin/repro --tg-config tg.json
- Quick mem usage sampling (dev): watch -n 0.5 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,name --format=csv'

Next actions & owners:
- (Ava) land canary flag and rollout to canary cluster (ETA: 2026-02-20)
- (Ethan) add prometheus metrics for per-stream pending_free_queue (ETA: 2026-02-25)
- (Priya) implement dedicated slab config for fused-attention model families (ETA: 2026-03-04)
- (Diego) reproduce deterministic failing sequence and create test harness (ENG-4321) (ETA: 2026-03-10)

Notes: this doc is intentionally informal; please append experiments/links as you run them. If you find an alternative root cause with stronger evidence, replace the hypothesis section and mark status accordingly.

End of file.
